problem_context.statement: Given a string containing only the characters (, ), [, ], {, and }, return true when every opening bracket is closed by the same bracket type in the correct nesting order.

examples.explanation: Each opener is matched in reverse opening order.
The closing parenthesis does not match the most recent opener.

problem_context.title: Valid Parentheses
constraints: s contains only the six bracket characters described above.

expected_approaches.summary: Push the closing bracket expected for each opener; every closer must match the stack top.
expected_approaches.applicability: Properly nested delimiter languages with finitely many bracket types.
assumptions: Input is restricted to supported bracket characters.
key_invariants: The stack top is the only closing bracket that can legally appear next.
common_implementation_variants: push openers and map closers back to them
common_failure_modes: forgetting unmatched openers at the end

alternative_approaches.summary: Push opening brackets and verify each closer against the matching opener.
alternative_approaches.applicability: Equivalent stack formulation when a closer-to-opener map is clearer.
key_invariants: The stack holds unmatched opening brackets in nesting order.
tradeoffs: Needs an explicit matching map on closing input.
common_failure_modes: comparing against the wrong mapping direction

reference_solutions.source_code: class Solution { public: bool isValid(string s){ vector<char> expected; for(char c:s){ if(c=='(') expected.push_back(')'); else if(c=='[') expected.push_back(']'); else if(c=='{') expected.push_back('}'); else { if(expected.empty()||expected.back()!=c) return false; expected.pop_back(); } } return expected.empty(); } };

class Solution { public boolean isValid(String s){ java.util.Deque<Character> expected=new java.util.ArrayDeque<>(); for(char c:s.toCharArray()){ if(c=='(') expected.push(')'); else if(c=='[') expected.push(']'); else if(c=='{') expected.push('}'); else { if(expected.isEmpty()||expected.pop()!=c) return false; } } return expected.isEmpty(); } }

invariants.diagnostic_goal: The top expected closer corresponds to the most recently unmatched opener.

complexity_expectations.diagnostic_goal: Explain one push or pop per bracket and the worst-case nesting storage.

common_misconceptions.diagnostic_goal: Balanced totals alone do not prove correct nesting.

failure_modes.diagnostic_goal: Reject a closer before any compatible opener.
Reject nonempty stack after processing all input.

edge_cases.diagnostic_goal: Reject a closer that violates last-opened-first-closed order.

counterexamples.purpose: The first closer has no opener.
Unresolved opening brackets remain at the end.

constraint_mutations.diagnostic_goal: Extend the mapping while preserving the same nesting invariant.

probe_opportunities.diagnostic_goal: Defend why the latest unmatched opener determines the only legal next closer.
Test why an empty final stack is necessary as well as sufficient with per-character checks.

sample_phrasings: Why must this closing bracket match the most recent opener?

expected_good_signals: rejects when no expected closer exists
weak_or_misconception_signals: underflows or accepts a premature closer
sample_phrasings: What does your code do when the first character is a closing bracket?

expected_good_signals: requires an empty stack at end
weak_or_misconception_signals: accepts a string ending with openers
sample_phrasings: What remaining state must be true after the final character?

level_considerations.guidance: Focus on matching type and nesting order.
Expect a defensible stack invariant and boundary handling.

pack.reference_reasoning: The expected-closing stack is the reviewed primary formulation, while equivalent opener-stack implementations remain valid when they preserve the same nesting invariant.

input.candidate_statement: I only need equal counts of opening and closing brackets.

technical_rationale_rubric.technical_issue: Ask the candidate to test the count-only rule against ordering or type mismatch.

review.description: A count-only parenthesis claim needs a counterexample diagnostic.
